messages.author: 7e479f2f6ea3ce13
messages.subject: comment.char argument disappeared from read.csv.sql (?)
parts:
Hi all,

using the newest development version, I seem to be unable to use the comment.char argument. Is this intentional, and if so what is considered a comment character, if anything?

Thanks,

Peter

messages.author: 17e30776ec2a7fb1
messages.subject: Re: comment.char argument disappeared from read.csv.sql (?)
parts:
comment.char seemed to be involved in one of the incompatabilities with the new RSQLite 1.0.0 and has been removed in order not to hold up 0.4-10 until I find the time to track it down.

You can use the filter argument in the interim, e.g.

     read.csq.sql(...whatever..., filter = 'sed -e "s/ *#.*//" ')

(If you are on Windows note that sed is available in Rtools.)

That example using filter should be exactly equivalent to using comment.char="#".  Note that it is not a new feature.  sqldf has had the filter argument for quite some time, maybe years.

If you can wait a bit I do intend to put the comment.char feature back but I was concerned that it was holding up all uses of read.csv.sql so at least now it works as before in most cases and there is the indicated workaround for anyone who needs to remove comments.

messages.author: 17e30776ec2a7fb1
messages.subject: Re: comment.char argument disappeared from read.csv.sql (?)
parts: Just a follow up.  I have looked into it a bit and the comment.char argument that was in prior versions of sqldf was passed to RSQLite but RSQLite did not actually do anything with it -- RSQLite's import  functionality never had the capability to remove comments.  Thus the main change that has caused problems seems to be just that RSQLite no longer accepts arguments that it does not implement.  When using sqldf the way to remove comments is by using the filter= argument and it seems that this was always the case.  Should RSQLite implement a comment.char in the future then I hope to provide this in sqldf as well.
